acip: JI LTA BA DE LTAR DU, MI SDUG PA'I YID CAN GYI RNAL 'BYOR PA LTAR CIG SHOS TE RNAL 'BYOR PA MA YIN PAS, RNAL 'BYOR BAS KENG RUS MTHONG BA'I YUL DER BLO GTAD PA STE KENG RUS LA SOGS PA'I YUL LA LTA 'DOD PA RNAMS LA YANG KENG RUS RTOGS PA STE MTHONG BA SKYE BAR 'GYUR TE, SNGON PO SOGS KYI RNAM SHES BZHIN NO,,
english: Just so—in the same way—we can have a case where there is a certain other individual who is not a deep practitioner; which is to say, they are not like the deep practitioner whose mind has taken on an aspect of the repulsive. It should be the case then that if they decide they would like to look upon the skeletons (or whatever else it may be)—if they were to direct their minds towards the same objects where the deep practitioner perceives skeletons—then a perception of the skeletons, that sight, should also arise in them. It would be just the same as the perception of blue and the like.
